documents/admissions/2027-admission-crit.text: Admission Criteria - Entry to Year 7 in September 2027 Archbishop Tenison’s is a mixed comprehensive school, in the London Borough of Croydon and the Anglican Diocese of Southwark, for pupils aged 11-18. Places in Year 7 are allocated largely on the basis of church membership, with 25% of places allocated to feeder schools and 25% of places open to all. No entrance examination is set. Ethos Statement: Archbishop Tenison’s Church of England School has a distinctive Christian ethos which gives the school its purpose and provides an inclusive environment where children can learn and flourish in a setting shaped by Christian values. We welcome applications from all members of the community and we ask all parents to respect the Christian ethos of the school. 1. Places Available The Governing Body is responsible for the admission of pupils to Archbishop Tenison’s Church of England School and will admit 150 pupils to Year 7 in September. This admission number has been agreed between the Governing Body and the Local Authority and applies to the year 2027. 50% of available places are Foundation Places (see 11. below). 50% of available places are Open Places (see 12. below). All applicants must complete a Common Application Form (CAF) supplied by their Local Authority and name this school on the form to be considered for a place. Foundation Place applicants and Open Place Feeder School applicants must also complete a Supplementary Information Form (SIF) and return it to the School by the closing date. Open Place applicants for Local Places do not need to complete a SIF. 2. Access The school has no specific units or facilities for pupils with particular special needs and no specific facilities for pupils with physical disabilities. The School is on a level site but much accommodation, including some specialist rooms, is on the first and second floors. There is one lift – in an external building. Lifts (which would require Government funding) were included in the plans put forward by the Governors for the last building extension, but unfortunately deleted by the Department for Education on the grounds of cost. As far as possible within the limitations of the premises, the school will ensure that pupils with disabilities have access to the same opportunities as other pupils. 3. Area Served by the School Priority is given to children who live within the Archdeaconry of Croydon and the Deanery of Sutton. A map showing this area is available on the school’s website. 4. How Distance is Measured Where places are offered according to the nearness of the home to the school, the distance will be measured in a straight line from the child’s home address to the designated entrance(s) of the school using a computerised measuring system (GIS) and geographical reference points as provided by the National Land and Property Gazetteer (NLPG). Those living closer to the school will receive higher priority. If a child lives in a shared property such as flats, the geographical references will determine the start point within the property boundaries to be used for distance calculation purposes. Tiebreaker: - where the distance is identical for two or more applicants, the drawing of lots is used as a final arbiter. This will be independently verified. 5. Context In order to preserve equality of opportunity for children who live in different family structures, the application process concerns the child seeking a place and ONE named parent or carer. It is for the applicant family to choose which parent’s or carer’s details are to be included on the application form. In order to meet the conditions (section 11. below) for offering places when the number of applicants is more than the number of Foundation Places, the named parent or carer should normally be the parent or carer (when there is more than one in the family structure) whose minister can certify that they are practising members of their church or congregation. 6. Definitions For the purpose of this Admission Policy: ‘Family’ refers to the child and the ONE named parent or carer mentioned above with whom the child is normally resident. ‘Sibling’ refers to brothers and sisters (blood relatives), step-siblings, adopted and long-term foster children living at the same address. A ‘Looked After Child’ is a child who is (a) in the care of a Local Authority, or (b) being provided with accommodation by a Local Authority in the exercise of their social services functions (see definition in section 22(1) of the Children Act 1989) at the time of applying to the school. A ‘Previously Looked After Child’ is a child who was looked after immediately prior to being adopted, including Internationally Adopted Previously Looked After Children (IAPLAC). or who became subject to a child arrangement order under the Children & Families Act 2014, or special guardianship order. The Governors will require written confirmation (e.g. through written confirmation from the Local Authority) that the child is looked after, or previously looked after, and will be so at the time of making an application to the school. ‘Involvement’ is any activity (practical, social, educational, cultural or spiritual) which is an outward expression of the family’s participation in the life of the church to which they belong. It excludes any practical or financial support given to the school or any associated organisation, including any religious authority. Where percentages used in this policy do not produce whole numbers, 0.5 or more will be rounded up and less than 0.5 will be rounded down. 7. Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCP’s) Parents of pupils who have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) are required to apply for school places separately through the Local Authority, from whom advice is available. If a child with an EHCP, is placed in the school by the local authority before the normal admission round, the number of places available to other applicants will be reduced. The Governors will admit all those pupils whose EHCP, names the School (All schools are consulted by the LA prior to the school being named). 8. Looked After Children The highest priority is given to Looked After and Previously Looked After Children – with supporting evidence from their Local Authority (as defined in section 6 above). 9. Exceptional and professionally supported medical or social need. This must be supported by written evidence at the time of application, e.g. from a specialist health professional, social worker or other care professional. The evidence must set out the reasons why this school is the most suitable school and the difficulties that would be caused if the child had to attend another school. 10. Children of Staff Children of staff include full, step, half, adopted and fostered children living in the same household as the member of staff employed by the school on a permanent full-time or fractional contract in either of the following circumstances: (i) The member of staff has been employed for two years or more before the admission application and is still employed, without having given notice or been given notice that the employment will end, at the time the offer is made. (ii) The member of staff is recruited to fill a vacant teaching post for which there is a demonstrable skill shortage (determined by the Headteacher with the Chair of Governors). 11. Foundation Places (based on Church Membership) The Governing Body has designated 50% of available places as Foundation Places, after any children admitted who have an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan which names the school (see section 7 above), Looked After and Previously Looked After Children (see section 8 above), Children of Staff and Governors’ Places (see section 13 below). a) Definitions of Churches from which Children are Admitted In addition to children of Church of England Families, places are also offered to children whose Family belongs to a church which is a full member of one or more of the following organisations: Churches Together in England (CTE),The Evangelical Alliance (EA), Affinity or Fellowship of Independent Evangelical Churches (FIEC) at the time of application, and who live in the area defined in section 3 above. 50% of available places will be reserved for members of the Anglican Church and other churches defined above in this section. b) Evidence of Church Membership (i) The school will check official lists to see whether the applicant’s church comes within the groups mentioned in section 11a above. If they are not listed, applicants will need to supply evidence that their church is a member of one of these groups. (ii) In addition, whether Anglican or not, confirmation of membership of the applicant’s Family in the relevant church will be sought from the priest or minister concerned, who will also be required to give a reference in writing stating the frequency of church attendance by the Family, and give information about the involvement of the Family in church life. The school may contact the priest or minister for further clarification. c) Oversubscription Criteria for Foundation Places In the event of the school being oversubscribed by applicants, priority will be given to those who live in the area defined in section 3 above and who belong to a church included in section 11a above; places will be allocated according to the following conditions in order with applications from members of the Anglican Church given priority over those from other churches mentioned in 11a. (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) Children who attend church worship weekly with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer is actively involved with them in church life. “Actively involved” indicates that this activity is likely to be frequent (at least fortnightly), well established (for at least 1 year) and to carry with it some responsibility within the church. (iii) Children who attend church worship fortnightly with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer is actively involved with them in church life. “Actively involved” indicates that this activity is likely to be frequent (fortnightly), well established (for at least 1 year) and carry with it some responsibility within the church. (iv) Children who attend church worship weekly, fortnightly or less frequently with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer has some involvement with them in church life. “Some involvement” indicates that this activity is likely to be less frequent (monthly), less well established (for less than a year) and more passive (e.g. attending a meeting). (v) Children who attend church with the named parent or carer. Note: In any of the categories 11c (i- v) above where there are more applicants than places remaining available, places will be offered to the children whose named parent or carer has the greater level of responsibility and involvement. Where two or more named parents or carers have an identical level of responsibility and involvement, places will be offered according to the nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3 above. Unsuccessful applicants for Foundation Places will be considered under the Open Place criteria. If the Foundation Places overall are undersubscribed, those remaining unfilled will become Open Places. Parents are asked to note that because Scouts and Guides are frequently more secular than religious organisations, membership of these groups will not be regarded as active involvement, unless it can be clearly demonstrated that it is an integral part of church life. 12. Open Places The Governing Body has designated 50% of the available places as Open Places after any children admitted who have an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan which names the school (see 7 above), Looked After and Previously Looked After Children (see 8. above), Children of Staff and Governors’ Places. In the event of the School being oversubscribed by Open Place applicants, priority will be given to those who live in the area defined in section 3 (above) and who are not offered a Foundation Place, but whose parents have chosen the school for the type of education it provides. Parents applying for an Open Place should do so knowing that the purpose of the school is to provide an education based on Christian principles, and that the Governing Body is keen for all pupils to take part in the Christian worship of the school and to attend religious education lessons. a) Feeder Schools Half of the Open places (i.e. 25% of available places) are reserved for applications for children from the following Primary schools: a. St John’s Church of England Primary School, Shirley b. The Minster Church of England Primary School, Croydon c. St Mark’s Church of England Primary Academy, South Norwood d. Christ Church Church of England Primary School, Purley e. All Saints Church of England Primary School, Upper Norwood f. Coulsdon Church of England Primary School, Coulsdon g. Holy Trinity Church of England Primary School, Sutton h. All Saints Carshalton Church of England Primary School, Carshalton i. All Saints Benhilton Church of England Primary School, Sutton j. St Dunstan’s Church of England Primary School, Cheam If the number of applicants exceeds 25% places will be allocated according to the following criteria: (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) Remaining places will be allocated in strict rotation between applications for children from the above schools which must be specified on the Supplementary Information Form (SIF). Where the number of applications from a school exceeds the places allocated to that school then places will be offered according to the nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3 above. If the places reserved for applications for children from the above feeder schools are undersubscribed they will then become Local Places. b) Local Places Half of the Open places (i.e. 25% of available places) are open for applications for any child. If the number of applicants exceeds 25%, places will be allocated according to the following criteria: (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) The nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3. 13. Governors’ Places Governors may allocate a small number of places on compassionate grounds for social and medical need or for a child attending church regularly but unsupported by family. Those applying under this category should state this on the Supplementary Information Form (SIF) at the time of application and supply in writing relevant supporting professional evidence. Governors are able to allocate compassionate places irrespective of whether the school is oversubscribed by applicants who meet the criteria listed. Allocation of such places does not set a precedent for future applications as each case is treated on its own merits. 14. Education out of Normal (Chronological) Age Group Children are normally educated in school with others of their age group; however, in exceptional circumstances parents/carers may seek a place outside of their child’s normal age group. Decisions will be made on the basis of the circumstances of each case and in the best interests of the child. Account will be taken of the child’s academic, social and emotional development, whether they have previously been educated out of their normal age group and, where relevant, their medical history. Parents/carers must state clearly why they feel admission to a different year group is in the child's best interests and may provide recent professional evidence to support this. 15. Fair Access Protocol Archbishop Tenison’s School, in common with all other schools in Croydon, will admit pupils referred under the Fair Access Protocol, whom the school is directed to accept, even if this means going over number in a particular year group and even if there are other pupils on the waiting list. The other criteria detailed in this document do not apply to such pupils. 16. Waiting Lists The school operates a waiting list system, and those who are unsuccessful in their application will be offered the opportunity to have their child’s name placed on the relevant waiting list for a Foundation or Open Place. Any additional application received will require the list to be ranked again, in line with the published oversubscription criteria and places will be allocated according to the priorities described above. The waiting list for Year 7 will be maintained for at least one term after September 2027. 17. Late Applications The school will follow the common policy of the London Borough of Croydon in dealing with late applications. 18. In-Year Applications Applications for places outside the normal admission round and for other year groups may be made via the Local Authority with an In-Year Common Application Form. Those wishing to apply for a place under the Foundation Place or Feeder School criteria must also complete a supplementary information form (SIF) and return this directly to the school. 19. Sixth Form Admissions Admissions criteria for external applicants wishing to attend the Archbishop Tenison’s Sixth Form are published on the school website and available from the school office. 20. Supplementary Information Form (SIF) Failure to return the Supplementary Information Form (SIF) by the published deadline will mean that applicants cannot be considered for a place under the Foundation Place criteria or the Feeder School criteria, and the application will be dealt with under the Local Place criteria. 21. Appeals Parents who are not offered a place for their child at Archbishop Tenison’s CE High School have the right to appeal to an independent Appeal Panel. Parents wishing to appeal against the decision of their child not being offered a place should request an Appeal Pack from the Admissions Officer at the school in writing, either by letter or email, stating the child’s full name, date of birth and postal address. Should some appeals be unsuccessful, the Governing Body will not consider further applications from those parents within the same academic year unless there have been significant and material changes in their circumstances. Academic excellence for each person in a Christian community Archbishop Tenison’s Church of England High School, Selborne Road, Croydon, CR0 5JQ. www. archten.croydon.sch.uk 24/02/2026

documents/letters/whole-school-school-ex.text: 11th March 2026 Dear Parents and Carers Expectations - Behaviour As we approach the halfway point of the term, we are pleased to share that overall, things are going well and pupils continue to settle positively into school routines. Over the past few weeks, we have been successfully working with pupils to promote high expectations around behaviour, respect and responsibility across the school community. Our aim is not only to support pupils during the school day, but also to help them develop positive habits and routines that will extend beyond the school setting. As part of this work, we continue to focus on maintaining a safe, calm and respectful atmosphere for everyone. To support this, we are reinforcing the high standards of personal conduct we expect from all pupils while they are on the school site. One of the things we have recently noticed, is that some pupils engage in what they describe as “play fighting.” While this is often intended in a playful and friendly way, it can sometimes lead to accidental injuries or misunderstandings between pupils. It is therefore important that pupils understand the risks involved with physical contact and behave in a way that keeps themselves and others safe. For this reason, play fighting and rough physical behaviour are not permitted in school. Any incidents of such behaviour will be addressed promptly in line with the school’s behaviour policy. By maintaining these clear expectations, we can continue to ensure that the school remains a safe, calm, and welcoming environment for all pupils. We would greatly appreciate your support in reminding your child about these expectations and encouraging them to make positive choices when interacting with others at school. Thank you for your continued support. Yours sincerely Mr Koramoa Deputy Headteacher

documents/letters/whole-school-ski-trip-.text: 10th June 2026 Dear Parents and Carers Ski Trip to Italy 2027 I am delighted to be able to get in contact with you regarding the ski trip in 2027. Mr Winter has successfully run previous iterations of this trip over the past few years and I am really excited to take over and continue running the ski trip at Archbishop Tenisons. The 2027 ski trip to Italy will take place from the Saturday 6h – Friday 12th March 2027. This year’s ski trip was a great success, and we are very pleased to be able to offer another competitively priced ski trip in conjunction with ‘The Ski Company’ and partnering with Trinity CoE school in Lewisham, who we had a very positive experience with over previous years. ‘The Ski Company’ who have a real passion for skiing for all, and as part of our commitment to educating the whole pupil, feel that this is a fantastic opportunity to build cultural capital and to develop pupils social skills and physical fitness, as well as enabling pupils to experience environments outside of their normal day-to-day lives. Please find further information regarding the ski trip, location and how to pay via the following link: ARCHTEN | The Ski Company Summary as follows: Trip Dates: Resort: Ski Company: Cost: Deposit: Saturday, 6th March– Friday, 12th March 2027 Hotel Villagio Nevada – Costa – Alpe Cimbra ‘The Ski Company’ - ARCHTEN | The Ski Company £1285 per pupil £133.00 followed by 9 monthly payments of £128.00. Final balance is due on Monday 1st March 2027 The cost includes: • Return travel including flights and transport to and from airports • Full board accommodation • 5-day ski pass • Ski lessons 5 hours per day for 5 days • Local Italian ski school • Hire of all ski equipment • Evening activities • Winter sports insurance Not included: • Drinks except with meals • Pocket money • Specialist clothing and ski wear Payment Schedule To secure a place for your son/daughter, please pay a deposit on the attached link: ARCHTEN | The Ski Company The whole booking process is supported by ‘The Ski Company’. I will run two pre trip evenings which will be able to give more specific logistics, such as a kit list, timings for the trip and daily schedule once we are there. For current Year 11 only - Please note that students who meet the entry criteria for Archbishop Tenison's Sixth Form and will be joining us in September are eligible to sign up for this trip. Please do not hesitate to get back to me with any further questions. Kind regards, Mr Herbert Mr L Herbert Head of PE

documents/letters/whole-school-social-me.text: 23rd February 2026 Dear Parents/Carers, Over the half-term we have been made aware of an image currently circulating on social media, primarily Snapchat. Some of you have also contacted us about this, not surprisingly concerned about its content. The image refers to several local secondary schools, seeking to place them into opposing “Red” and “Blue” groups, and to encourage conflict between young people on this basis. All schools have received this communication from Croydon Police: "We are aware of social media posts currently circulating among students across several boroughs which appear to place certain schools on opposing ‘sides’. At this stage we have no intelligence to suggest planned violence or organised disorder; however, we are monitoring the situation ... Please ensure that staff are aware so they can monitor pupil behaviour, discourage the sharing of these posts, and pass on any concerns. We ask that schools do not circulate the material to students, but that duty staff remain alert during arrival and dismissal periods.” Their advice is: “Any safeguarding concerns or relevant information can be passed directly to your Neighbourhood Policing Team contact, via 101 or Crimestoppers.” They have also assured us as follows: "We will continue to monitor these posts, inform our local partners particularly in the areas listed and will respond accordingly to ensure there is a proportionate policing presence should that be required.” As a school we have spoken with the police directly and will continue to do so, as needed. We will keep up our daily duties and support for pupils as they travel to and from school. We do not want anyone’s schooling to be disrupted by things such as this. We encourage you as parents and carers to monitor your child’s social media activity and to speak with them about safe and responsible on-line conduct. Pupils should avoid engaging with, sharing, or responding to this content. They should go straight home after school and keep well clear of any events or gatherings referenced in these posts. We will contact you if there is any further information to pass on. Thank you for your continued support in helping us maintain a safe, calm and positive environment for our school community. Our shared vigilance is important in a situation like this. Yours sincerely, Richard Parrish Headteacher

documents/letters/year-11-y11-exam-resul.text: 28th April 2026 Dear Parents and Carers, Information for Parents and Pupils – New Exam Results App The Department for Education (DfE) has introduced a new Education Record app, which allows pupils to access their exam results digitally and securely. What is the app? The app gives pupils a personal digital record of their qualifications, including GCSE results, which can be accessed on their phone once results are released. This will help them when enrolling in sixth form or college and later when sharing qualifications with employers or training providers. Who can access it? Please note that the app is designed for pupils, not parents. Results will continue to be issued by the school in the usual way on results day, but pupils will later be able to view their results independently through the app. What pupils need to do now: We are asking pupils to download the app in advance, ready for sign-up in school: • Search for 'Education Record England' on the Apple App Store or Google Play Store • Download the app onto their phone What will happen in school: We will organise time in school for pupils to complete their sign-up. During this session: • A member of staff will support them • Pupils will scan a QR code issued by the school • This will securely link the app to their education record No results are released through the app until the official results date. We will share further details with pupils directly, and there is no action required from parents at this stage beyond encouraging pupils to download the app. Thank you for your continued support. Yours sincerely, Mr Miles Winter Senior Assistant Headteacher - Curriculum, Learning, Assessment, and Progress

documents/letters/year-11-y11-gcse-arran.text: 30th April 2026 Dear Year 11 Parents and Carers Year 11 GCSE Exam Arrangements I am writing to inform you about the arrangements for Year 11 pupils up until half term, once the GCSE exams begin. From Tuesday, 5th May to Friday, 8th May, pupils will be in school as usual and attend normal timetabled lessons. The only exceptions will be for those pupils who study German, Latin and Drama as they will sit their exams in the school hall on the following dates: Thursday, 7th May – German Friday, 8th May – Latin (am) & Drama (pm) The majority of GCSE exams begin the week beginning Monday, 11th May. The expectation is that pupils who have a morning exam, which is all pupils on most days, arrive to school in good time, ideally before 8.30am. Pupils should line up outside the school hall by 8.40am. If pupils do not have an afternoon exam, they will then be dismissed and allowed to study and revise at home. If pupils do have an afternoon exam, they will be expected to remain in school, go to break as normal at the end of their exam and will attend revision sessions during periods 3 and 4. If pupils do not have a morning exam, they should arrive to school between 11am and 11.15am if they wish to attend revision sessions during periods 3 and 4. If they do not wish to attend the revision sessions, they should arrive in school between 12.50pm and 1.10pm. Pupils will not be admitted into the school during periods 3 and 4 (ie between 11.15am to 12.45pm). Revision sessions will be led by subject teachers prior to their exam, usually for that afternoon. Where subjects are running revision sessions before their morning exam, these will usually start at 8am and pupils will be informed directly by their subject teachers. Scheduled revision sessions (periods 3 and 4): Tuesday, 12th May Biology (for all pupils) Wednesday, 13th May Computer Science Thursday, 14th May German Friday, 15th May Latin Tuesday, 19th May Computer Science Wednesday, 20th May RS Thursday, 21st May Latin Year 11 pupils will be able to purchase lunch from the school canteen if they wish at the earlier time of 12.45pm. They should then line up for their afternoon exam at 1.20pm, as the exam will begin at 1.30pm. Pupils who do not have an afternoon exam will be dismissed at 12.45pm to maximise their independent study and revision at home. I will write to you again before half term with the specific arrangements for the exams taking place after half term. Following the end of the GCSE exams, there will be a celebratory event in school (date to be confirmed) with light refreshments and an opportunity for pupils to sign shirts and receive their leavers hoodies. Please note that all Year 11 pupils should wear full school uniform throughout the exam period and whenever they are in school. documents/letters/year-7-multi-activity-.text: 18th March 2026 Dear Parents and Carers Peak District Multi Activity Trip Visit Monday, 29th June to Thursday, 2nd July 2026 We have an exciting opportunity for your child to join a group of Year 7 and 8 pupils on a Multi Activity visit to the Peak District, at the end of the summer term. The aim of the visit will be to build pupils confidence and resilience, as well as learning new skills, whilst giving them a taste of outdoor activities. The location of the Peak District should provide an amazing setting to achieve some fantastic experiences. Pupils will take part in a number of activities in well-known walking and climbing areas around the world famous Stanage Edge gritstone outcrop. These activities include hill walking, scrambling, caving, bouldering and rock climbing. We will stay in a self-catering bunkhouse in Hathersage, Hope Valley, where pupils will help prepare and cook some of their own food. All instructors are DBS checked and hold all the appropriate climbing and guide qualifications. The company (Venture Elements) has liability insurance, which covers the group activities whilst under instruction and supervision. Pupils will get two half days of activities on travel days and 2 full days of activities in between. We will have full days of physical activities, which will push pupils physically and improve their skills and confidence. Activities can be modified for disability, please contact me if you have queries about accessibility. Previous experience and purchasing of equipment is not necessary. Cost and Availability Spaces are limited and will be offered on a first come first served basis The cost of the visit is £325.00 per pupil, which includes travel, accommodation, food instruction and equipment costs. Pupils will need to bring a packed lunch on the first day. A non-refundable deposit of £100.00 is required to secure a place for your child. Please note that if pupils decide not to attend, we will not be able to issue a refund unless another pupil is able to fill the place. Please make payment of £100.00 via MCAS/Trips under the relevant group for your son or daughter by Friday, 16th April 2026. The remaining £225.00 can be paid in installments but must be paid for in full by Friday, 12th June at the latest. Itinerary Monday, 29th June 8am 12.30pm- 1pm -5pm- Arrive to school and depart to the Peak District, Arrive at Stanage (pupils should bring their own packed lunch) Outdoor activity at Stanage Edge and return to bunkhouse in Hathersage for dinner Tuesday, 30th June - Wednesday, 1st July 10am-5pm- Breakfast at the bunkhouse followed by outdoor activity around the Stanage and Burbage areas. Packed lunch provided. Thursday, 2nd July 9am – 1pm- Breakfast at the bunkhouse and followed by outdoor activity around the Hope Valley 2pm - Depart Peak District 6:30pm (approx.) - Arrive back at School where pupils will be dismissed Dinner will be provided at the bunkhouse each evening. Evening activities will be a movie night, camp fires and an evening walk on the top of Stanage Edge. Kit List A kit list will be sent out with a final letter prior to departure. I very much hope your son or daughter will be interested in participating in this wonderful opportunity. I look forward to hearing from you. If you have any questions regarding details of the trip, please get in contact with me via - crokn@archten.croydon.sch.uk Yours sincerely Mr N Coker Mr N Croker Head of Year 13 and Teacher of Geography Useful Questions and Answers This is a list of questions you might wish to ask when considering allowing your child on the school multi activity Trip. Can you explain the sorts of activities you are able to offer? The pupils will undertake a mixture of hill walking, scrambling, caving, bouldering and rock climbing throughout the activity days. Are they suitable for my child(ren)? The activity will be tailored to the ability of the group. While it is important to stretch the pupils, at no time will they be placed in a situation where their lack of ability places them in danger. Are the people taking my child on activities competent to do so? The school have employed private instructors for all activities. They hold the MIC,MIA and IML awards which are the highest UK and international mountaineering awards available. These awards give the instructors the remit to undertake supervision of groups for all the activities we will be undertaking. What child protection procedures are in place? The pupils will be accompanied by a member of ABT staff at all times and the schools normal child protection policies will apply. · What sorts of insurance do you have? The instructors have their own liability insurance which has been vetted by the school. This covers the liability of group instruction for the activities which we will be undertaking. · Do you have emergency procedures? – What are they? Both the instructors and Mr Croker hold Outdoor First Aid awards and are trained to deal with emergency situations and first aid in outdoor environments.

documents/letters/year-9-year-9-assessme.text: 2nd March 2026 Dear Parents and Carers Year 9 Assessments – Week Commencing Monday, 20th April 2026 I am writing to inform you about the plans for your child’s Spring assessment window. Year 9aAssessments will take place in the Hall. Due to the nature of the timetable, it is therefore not practical to issue actual timetables as there would be many different versions, however your child’s subject teacher will inform them of the exact time of their assessment. These assessments are a great opportunity for your child to showcase the knowledge, understanding and skills they have gained during their time at Tenison’s so far, as well as being an important opportunity to gain excellent quality feedback on how to progress further. All assessments will run under strict exam conditions to ensure pupils have the opportunity to produce their best work. The subjects that will be assessed are:  Art  Computer Science  Drama  English  French  Geography  German  History  Latin  Maths  P.E  Religious Studies  Science Please find below the list of topics that will form the basis of your child’s assessments and therefore should be the focus of their revision:  Art: Human Rights  Computer Science: Cyber security, Representing Images and Sound, Python Programming, Computational Thinking  Drama: Section A: Theatre Makers roles and Vocabulary Section B: Live Theatre Evaluation  English: Macbeth  French: Module 1: Mon monde á moi Module 2: Projets d’ avenir Module 3: Ma vie en musique  Geography: Antarctica: Living off the Earth’s resources; Ecosystems; Climate Change (please note that as these assessments are end of year assessments, they will contain questions from a number of topics)  German: Module 1: My Role Model, Parts of the Body, what have you done in your life (past tense with sein and haben), Module 2: Music, Future plans, what instruments you play, Making comparisons (Comparative and superlative), Past tense (Separable verbs and non-separable verbs), Question words.  History: World War One, the Suffrage Movement, The Holocaust, World War ll turning points.  Latin: Cambridge Latin Course Stages 10-12, Roman Families and Relationships (including literature)  Maths: Properties of Number, Percentages, Area and Volume, Equations, Inequalities and Formulae, Fractions, Rates, Standard form, Maths and Money, Straight Line Graphs, Ratio and Proportion, Constructions and Congruence, Similarity, Algebraic Manipulation.  Physical Education: Immediate; Short and long-term effects of exercise; Components of Fitness; Types of training; Muscles; Bones; Principles of training.  Religious Studies and Theology: Selected questions from all topics studied this year - Philosophy and Ethics.  Science:  Biology: Cells, Microscopes and Enzymes  Chemistry: Particles - states of matter and separation techniques  Physics: Motion and Energy The secret to great revision to test yourself so that you have to recall information from memory. Below are some ideas you can use to add variety and make revision more interesting: 1. Remembering Key Facts Help your child get things to stick in their memory. What Helps Quick Quizzes What It Means Testing themselves helps memory more than just reading notes. Little and Often Mixing Topics Pictures and Words Spreading revision out over time works better than cramming. Switching between subjects or topics helps the brain stay active. Using diagrams or drawings alongside notes helps memory. 2. Understanding Ideas Better Help your child make sense of what they’re learning. What Helps Explain It Back Real-Life Examples What It Means Talking through ideas helps them understand. Linking ideas to everyday life makes them clearer. Talk Through Mistakes Explaining why something was wrong helps learning. 3. Getting Ready for Exams Help your child feel confident and prepared. What You Can Do Ask them questions from flashcards or past papers. Let them try to answer before looking it up. Help them plan short sessions across the week, not all at once. Encourage them to revise different subjects in one evening. Help them turn notes into mind maps or labelled diagrams. What You Can Do Ask them to teach you a topic or explain how something works. Chat about how school topics show up in cooking, sports, or the news. Go through a question they got wrong and ask, “What would you do differently next time?” What Helps Practice Papers Learn from Mistakes Time Planning What It Means Doing past papers builds confidence. Reviewing errors helps improve. Knowing how long to spend on each question is key. What You Can Do Set up quiet, timed sessions. Praise effort, not just results. Help them spot patterns in what they get wrong and talk about how to fix it. Help them practice timing themselves and moving on when stuck. Teachers will have given your child more in-depth information regarding the assessment and will be placing revision materials and guidance on Teams for pupils to access, so please do encourage them to take their revision seriously. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact your child’s tutor in the first instance. Yours sincerely Mr Winter – Senior Assistant Headteacher

documents/news/headteacher-update.pdf.text: 2nd July 2026 Dear Parents and Carers As we approach the end of the school year, we wanted to communicate with you directly and bring you an update about the recruitment of a new Headteacher to succeed Mr Richard Parrish on his retirement at the end of August. After two national advertisements, several tours of the school and a good level of interest in the opportunity to become Headteacher of Archbishop Tenison’s, we received a good number of applications, held one round of interviews in March and then set up a second round in May. As we have not yet found the person we are looking for, we have now decided to advertise again after the summer. It is so important to all of us as Governors to appoint the right Headteacher for this school. In the meantime, from 1st September 2026 we are pleased to announce that Miss Akanho and Mr Koramoa, our two Deputy Headteachers, have kindly agreed to become Joint Interim Headteachers of the school until a new headteacher can be appointed. In this they will be ably supported by Mrs Gravett and Mr Winter, currently Senior Assistant Headteachers, who will both become Interim Deputy Headteachers. Other senior teaching staff have also agreed to take on additional responsibilities to make this work. Full details of what has been arranged will be shared with you before the end of term. Whilst we could have brought in an Interim Headteacher from outside the school to fill this gap in the short term, we quickly worked out it would be much better for the school to be ably led by the team of Senior Leaders currently in post, who know the school, its pupils and staff well. Following the recent OFSTED and SIAMS inspections the school has drawn up an Action Plan which these leaders are best placed to implement. As we enter the 2026-27 school year the school is in good shape and on a promising upward trajectory. From September the focus will be on ensuring that the new school year starts well and that the good work on the behaviour and culture, teaching and learning, assessment and progress, and on improving the school’s facilities and building up the Sixth Form in size can all continue. We have appointed most of the new teachers we need. A new Science Laboratory is to be created over the summer. The Caretaker’s Bungalow is being changed into a Pupil Support Centre, as part of Vision 312. The foyer in Reception is to be refurbished. We look forward to writing to you again before the end of term. Yours sincerely, Richard Parrish Headteacher

documents/news/letter-from-chair-of-gove.text: 22nd January 2026 Dear Parents and Carers, Following Mr Parrish's letter of 20 January, I am writing to advise of the action the Governors will be taking in the following weeks. I ask you to keep the Governing Body in your prayers as we undertake this very important task in the life of this school - and would ask for your prayers for Richard Parrish over the next 6 months and as he moves forward into this next stage of his life. Best wishes, Eileen P Chapman Chair of Governors

documents/pages/16-19-bursary-fund-guida.text: Archbishop Tenison’s 16 to 19 Bursary Fund 2025/26 Guidance Notes What is the 16-19 Bursary Fund? 16 to 19 bursary schemes were introduced to provide financial help to young people aged 16 to 19 who face financial barriers to participating in education or training, provided they meet agreed standards of attendance and behaviour. Who is eligible for the 16-19 Bursary Fund? The school offers two types of bursary. You can only apply for one type, depending on your personal circumstances. 1. The vulnerable bursary To be eligible for the vulnerable bursary you must meet all four of the following conditions: 1. attend Archbishop Tenison’s C of E High School 2. be starting Year 12 or 13 in September 2025 3. be aged between 16 and 18 on 31 August 2025 4. belong to one of the following groups: - young person in care, including unaccompanied asylum- seeking child - young care leaver; or - be receiving income support or universal credit in own right - be receiving Employment Support Allowance and are also in receipt of Disability Living Allowance or Personal Independence Payments. 2. The discretionary bursary To be eligible for the discretionary bursary you must meet four of the following conditions: 1. attend Archbishop Tenison’s C of E High School 2. be starting Year 12 or 13 in September 2025 3. be aged between 16 and 18 on 31 August 2025 4. living in a household with an annual income below £32,000 before tax and national insurance or receive free school meals 5. An accompanied asylum seeker How much money will I get? If you are eligible for the vulnerable bursary of up to £1,200 it will be released to you for specific educational reasons only. Please be advised that if eligible for financial support under the vulnerable bursary scheme, you will not automatically be awarded this amount. If there is limited financial need for assistance from the bursary you will be allocated reduced support, or in some instances where there is no financial need, no bursary will be awarded. Students will only receive the amount they actually need to participate in their studies and will not automatically be awarded £1,200 if they do not need the full amount. If you are eligible for the discretionary bursary you will not be allocated a specific amount, but your needs will be discussed with a relevant member of the Sixth Form team. This money will be used to support your educational studies. Students should not presume that funds will be released and must always ensure the ‘costs’ will be agreed before any payment is made. Receipts must be provided for purchases before payment can be made. What can I use the bursary for? The bursary is to help with costs related to your studies, for example tutor support, transport, books and equipment, and other costs associated with your course. Are there any conditions attached to the fund? You will be expected to: • have high attendance. You will not be eligible for the bursary if your attendance falls below the minimum requirements. Payments will not be backdated, • be punctual to the school every day • attend all sessions • meet academic targets and • adhere to the expectations placed on all Archbishop Tenison’s Sixth Form students. How do I apply? 1. Complete the attached application form. 2. Attach evidence of your financial or living situation to support your application. These must be the original documents, not photocopies. 3. Give the application to Mrs Yankah in the Sixth Form Office. She will copy documents and return your originals. When do I need to apply by and how will I hear the outcome? The deadline for applying is 31 October 2025. We will consider late applications but will consider these after we have processed all the applications received on time. We will write to everyone who applies to tell you the outcome of your application. We will also contact you if we need more information from you to process your application. What should I do if I’m not happy with your decision? Appeals against the decision must be made in writing to the Headteacher within 5 working days of receipt of the bursary notification. When will I be able to start using funds? When your application is approved, you can arrange to discuss the use with the designated person. How will you pay me? Where possible we will always aim to make the purchase for you. When this is not possible bursary payments can be made into your own bank account by a process called BACS transfer. It is essential that you have a bank account in your name as payments can only be made into your own account via a bank transfer. It is important that you make sure that your bank or building society can accept BACS transfer before you provide your bank account details. Post Office accounts and some Credit Unions do not accept BACS payments. Bursary money will be issued as discussed with the Sixth Form team. You will need to complete the Student Purchase Order Form and get it authorised prior to making a purchase. You will also need to provide receipts as proof of purchase. Failure to adhere to the correct procedure could lead to purchases not being refunded. The form will be available from the Sixth Form office. How long will I receive payments for? As long as you are adhering to all the conditions as stated in this document you will continue to be able to use your bursary allocation as agreed for the school year 2025/2026. New applications must be submitted for consideration every year. The terms of the scheme may change for school year 2026/2027. There is no guarantee that you will receive funding next year, even if you are eligible this year. Who do I contact if I have any questions? Speak to Mrs Yankah, Sixth Form Support and Administrator. Where can I get more information on the 16-19 Bursary Fund? General information on bursary funds are available on the Direct.Gov website – www.direct.gov.uk/en/EducationAndLearning/14to19/MoneyToLearn/16to19bursary/index.htm What happens if my financial or living circumstances change? If you have a change of personal circumstances such as a change of address or household income, you must let us know immediately in writing. If you change your bank account details, you must also write to us immediately. We will need to check your signature against your original application so we can only accept changes to banking details received by post. If you leave school before completing your course, your payments will be stopped. The information provided on the Bursary Application Form will be treated with confidentiality at all times and is covered by the data protection legislation. Please refer to our Privacy Notice on the school website. We will only retain your data for as long as necessary, after which time it will be securely destroyed.

documents/pages/2025-admission-criteria..text: Admission Criteria - Entry to Year 7 in September 2025 Archbishop Tenison’s is a mixed comprehensive school, in the London Borough of Croydon and the Anglican Diocese of Southwark, for pupils aged 11-18. Places in Year 7 are allocated largely on the basis of church membership, with 20% of places allocated to feeder schools and 20% of places open to all. No entrance examination is set. Ethos Statement: Archbishop Tenison’s Church of England School has a distinctive Christian ethos which gives the school its purpose and provides an inclusive environment where children can learn and flourish in a setting shaped by Christian values. We welcome applications from all members of the community and we ask all parents to respect the Christian ethos of the school. 1. Places Available The Governing Body is responsible for the admission of pupils to Archbishop Tenison’s Church of England School and will admit 150 pupils to Year 7 in September. This admission number has been agreed between the Governing Body and the Local Authority and applies to the year 2025. 60% of available places are Foundation Places (see 10. below). 40% of available places are Open Places (see 11. below). All applicants must complete a Common Application Form (CAF) supplied by their Local Authority and name this school on the form to be considered for a place. Foundation Place applicants and Open Place Feeder School applicants must also complete a Supplementary Information Form (SIF) and return it to the School by the closing date. Open Place applicants for Local Places do not need to complete a SIF. 2. Access The school has no specific units or facilities for pupils with particular special needs and no specific facilities for pupils with physical disabilities. The School is on a level site but much accommodation, including some specialist rooms, is on the first and second floors. There is one lift – in an external building. Lifts (which would require Government funding) were included in the plans put forward by the Governors for the last building extension, but unfortunately deleted by the Department for Education on the grounds of cost. As far as possible within the limitations of the premises, the school will ensure that pupils with disabilities have access to the same opportunities as other pupils. 3. Area Served by the School Priority is given to children who live within the Archdeaconry of Croydon and the Deanery of Sutton. A map showing this area is available on the school’s website. 4. How Distance is Measured Where places are offered according to the nearness of the home to the school, the distance will be measured in a straight line from the child’s home address to the designated entrance(s) of the school using a computerised measuring system (GIS) and geographical reference points as provided by the National Land and Property Gazetteer (NLPG). Those living closer to the school will receive higher priority. If a child lives in a shared property such as flats, the geographical references will determine the start point within the property boundaries to be used for distance calculation purposes. Tiebreaker: - where the distance is identical for two or more applicants, the drawing of lots is used as a final arbiter. This will be independently verified. 5. Context In order to preserve equality of opportunity for children who live in different family structures, the application process concerns the child seeking a place and ONE named parent or carer. It is for the applicant family to choose which parent’s or carer’s details are to be included on the application form. In order to meet the conditions (section 10. below) for offering places when the number of applicants is more than the number of Foundation Places, the named parent or carer should normally be the parent or carer (when there is more than one in the family structure) whose minister can certify that they are practising members of their church or congregation. 6. Definitions For the purpose of this Admission Policy: ‘Family’ refers to the child and the ONE named parent or carer mentioned above with whom the child is normally resident. ‘Sibling’ refers to brothers and sisters (blood relatives), step-siblings, adopted and long-term foster children living at the same address. A ‘Looked After Child’ is a child who is (a) in the care of a Local Authority, or (b) being provided with accommodation by a Local Authority in the exercise of their social services functions (see definition in section 22(1) of the Children Act 1989) at the time of applying to the school. A ‘Previously Looked After Child’ is a child who was looked after immediately prior to being adopted, including Internationally Adopted Previously Looked After Children (IAPLAC), or who became subject to a child arrangement order under the Children & Families Act 2014, or special guardianship order. The Governors will require written confirmation (e.g. through written confirmation from the Local Authority) that the child is looked after, or previously looked after, and will be so at the time of making an application to the school. ‘Involvement’ is any activity (practical, social, educational, cultural or spiritual) which is an outward expression of the family’s participation in the life of the church to which they belong. It excludes any practical or financial support given to the school or any associated organisation, including any religious authority. Where percentages used in this policy do not produce whole numbers, 0.5 or more will be rounded up and less than 0.5 will be rounded down. 7. Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCP’s) Parents of pupils who have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) are required to apply for school places separately through the Local Authority, from whom advice is available. If a child with an EHCP, is placed in the school by the local authority before the normal admission round, the number of places available to other applicants will be reduced. The Governors will admit all those pupils whose EHCP, names the School (All schools are consulted by the LA prior to the school being named). 8. Looked After Children The highest priority is given to Looked After and Previously Looked After Children – with supporting evidence from their Local Authority (as defined in section 6 above). 9. Exceptional and professionally supported medical or social need. This must be supported by written evidence at the time of application, e.g. from a specialist health professional, social worker or other care professional. The evidence must set out the reasons why this school is the most suitable school and the difficulties that would be caused if the child had to attend another school. 10. Foundation Places The Governing Body has designated 60% of available places as Foundation Places, after any children admitted who have an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan which names the school (see section 7 above), Looked After and Previously Looked After Children (see section 8 above) and Governors’ Places (see section 12 below). a) Definitions of Churches from which Children are Admitted In addition to children of Church of England Families, places are also offered to children whose Family belongs to a church which is a full member of one or more of the following organisations: Churches Together in England (CTE), The Evangelical Alliance (EA), Affinity or Fellowship of Independent Evangelical Churches (FIEC) at the time of application, and who live in the area defined in section 3 above. 60% of available places will be reserved for members of the Anglican Church and other churches defined above in this section. b) Evidence of Church Membership (i) The school will check official lists to see whether the applicant’s church comes within the groups mentioned in section 10a above. If they are not listed, applicants will need to supply evidence that their church is a member of one of these groups. (ii) In addition, whether Anglican or not, confirmation of membership of the applicant’s Family in the relevant church will be sought from the priest or minister concerned, who will also be required to give a reference in writing stating the frequency of church attendance by the Family, and give information about the involvement of the Family in church life. The school may contact the priest or minister for further clarification. c) Oversubscription Criteria for Foundation Places In the event of the school being oversubscribed by applicants, priority will be given to those who live in the area defined in section 3 above and who belong to a church included in section 10a above; places will be allocated according to the following conditions in order with applications from members of the Anglican Church given priority over those from other churches mentioned in 10a. (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) Children who attend church worship weekly with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer is actively involved with them in church life. “Actively involved” indicates that this activity is likely to be frequent (at least fortnightly), well established (for at least 1 year) and to carry with it some responsibility within the church. (iii) Children who attend church worship fortnightly with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer is actively involved with them in church life. “Actively involved” indicates that this activity is likely to be frequent (fortnightly), well established (for at least 1 year) and carry with it some responsibility within the church. (iv) Children who attend church worship weekly, fortnightly or less frequently with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer has some involvement with them in church life. “Some involvement” indicates that this activity is likely to be less frequent (monthly), less well established (for less than a year) and more passive (e.g. attending a meeting). (v) Children who attend church with the named parent or carer. Note: In any of the categories 10c (i- v) above where there are more applicants than places remaining available, places will be offered to the children whose named parent or carer has the greater level of responsibility and involvement. Where two or more named parents or carers have an identical level of responsibility and involvement, places will be offered according to the nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3 above. Unsuccessful applicants for Foundation Places will be considered under the Open Place criteria. If the Foundation Places overall are undersubscribed, those remaining unfilled will become Open Places. Parents are asked to note that because Scouts and Guides are frequently more secular than religious organisations, membership of these groups will not be regarded as active involvement, unless it can be clearly demonstrated that it is an integral part of church life. 11. Open Places The Governing Body has designated 40% of the available places as Open Places after any children admitted who have an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan which names the school (see 7 above), Looked After and Previously Looked After Children (see 8. above) and Governors’ Places. In the event of the School being oversubscribed by Open Place applicants, priority will be given to those who live in the area defined in section 3 (above) and who are not offered a Foundation Place, but whose parents have chosen the school for the type of education it provides. Parents applying for an Open Place should do so knowing that the purpose of the school is to provide an education based on Christian principles, and that the Governing Body is keen for all pupils to take part in the Christian worship of the school and to attend religious education lessons. a) Feeder Schools Half of the Open places (i.e. 20% of available places) are reserved for applications for children from the following Primary schools: a. St John’s Church of England Primary School, Shirley b. The Minster Church of England Primary School, Croydon c. St Mark’s Church of England Primary Academy, South Norwood d. Christ Church Church of England Primary School, Purley e. All Saints Church of England Primary School, Upper Norwood f. Coulsdon Church of England Primary School, Coulsdon g. Holy Trinity Church of England Primary School, Sutton h. All Saints Carshalton Church of England Primary School, Carshalton i. All Saints Benhilton Church of England Primary School, Sutton j. St Dunstan’s Church of England Primary School, Cheam If the number of applicants exceeds 20%, places will be allocated according to the following criteria: (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) Remaining places will be allocated in strict rotation between applications for children from the above schools which must be specified on the Supplementary Information Form (SIF). Where the number of applications from a school exceeds the places allocated to that school then places will be offered according to the nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3 above. If the places reserved for applications for children from the above feeder schools are undersubscribed, they will then become Local Places. b) Local Places Half of the Open places (i.e. 20% of available places) are open for applications for any child. If the number of applicants exceeds 20%, places will be allocated according to the following criteria: (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) The nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3. 12. Governors’ Places Governors may allocate a small number of places on compassionate grounds for social and medical need or for a child attending church regularly but unsupported by family. Those applying under this category should state this on the Supplementary Information Form (SIF) at the time of application and supply in writing relevant supporting professional evidence. Governors are able to allocate compassionate places irrespective of whether the school is oversubscribed by applicants who meet the criteria listed. Allocation of such places does not set a precedent for future applications as each case is treated on its own merits. 13. Admission out of Normal (Chronological) Age Group Children are normally educated in school with others of their age group; however, in certain circumstances parents/carers may seek a place outside of their child’s normal age group. Decisions will be made on the basis of the circumstances of each case and in the best interests of the child. Account will be taken of the child’s academic, social and emotional development, whether they have previously been educated out of their normal age group and, where relevant, their medical history. Parents/carers must state clearly why they feel admission to a different year group is in the child's best interests and may provide recent professional evidence to support this. 14. Fair Access Protocol Archbishop Tenison’s School, in common with all other schools in Croydon, will admit pupils referred under the Fair Access Protocol, whom the school is directed to accept, even if this means going over number in a particular year group and even if there are other pupils on the waiting list. The other criteria detailed in this document do not apply to such pupils. 15. Waiting Lists The school operates a waiting list system, and those who are unsuccessful in their application will be offered the opportunity to have their child’s name placed on the relevant waiting list for a Foundation or Open Place. Any additional application received will require the list to be ranked again, in line with the published oversubscription criteria and places will be allocated according to the priorities described above. The waiting list for Year 7 will be maintained for at least one term after September 2025. 16. Late Applications The school will follow the common policy of the London Borough of Croydon in dealing with late applications. 17. In-Year Applications Applications for places outside the normal admission round and for other year groups may be made via the Local Authority with an In-Year Common Application Form. Those wishing to apply for a place under the Foundation Place or Feeder School criteria must also complete a supplementary information form (SIF) and return this directly to the school. 18. Sixth Form Admissions Admissions criteria for external applicants wishing to attend the Archbishop Tenison’s Sixth Form are published on the school website and available from the school office. 19. Supplementary Information Form (SIF) Failure to return the Supplementary Information Form (SIF) by the published deadline will mean that applicants cannot be considered for a place under the Foundation Place criteria or the Feeder School criteria, and the application will be dealt with under the Local Place criteria. 20. Appeals Parents who are not offered a place for their child at Archbishop Tenison’s CE High School have the right to appeal to an independent Appeal Panel. Parents wishing to appeal against the decision of their child not being offered a place should request an Appeal Pack from the Admissions Officer at the school in writing, either by letter or email, stating the child’s full name, date of birth and postal address. Should some appeals be unsuccessful, the Governing Body will not consider further applications from those parents within the same academic year unless there have been significant and material changes in their circumstances. Academic excellence for each person in a Christian community Archbishop Tenison’s Church of England High School, Selborne Road, Croydon, CR0 5JQ. www. archten.croydon.sch.uk 01/02/2024

This year, many students achieved the targets they had been working towards, demonstrating both solid attainment and steady progress in their studies. Overall, the year group’s results are in line with national outcomes, and we are confident that we will continue to improve year on year. This consistency is a great achievement and a testament to the hard work of both our pupils and staff. Congratulations to pupils such as Hannah, Osakpolor, Simona, and Amelia, who achieved steadily in a number of subjects, including some excellent grades of 8 and 9. Their efforts, as with several of our pupils, have opened up a wide range of postGCSE opportunities. We are proud of all our Year 11 pupils for the commitment they have shown throughout the year. Meeting and exceeding their targets represents an important step forward, and we look forward to seeing them continue to grow academically and personally as they progress to the next stage of their education.

These results are a testament to the dedication, perseverance and academic ambition they have shown throughout their Sixth Form studies. Further congratulations go to James (ABB), Atigla (AABC) and Zain (AB and Distinction in Music), whose achievements reflect the breadth of talent and commitment within this year's cohort. We would also like to congratulate the many students who achieved strong results across a wide range of subjects, reflecting the breadth of opportunity available within our Sixth Form curriculum. These outcomes are a testament not only to the efforts of our students, but also to the support provided by staff, parents and carers throughout their studies. As a school community, we wish all of our Year 13 students every success as they move on amd are confident that they will continue to embody the values of Archbishop Tenison’s and make a positive contribution to the communities and institutions they join. Congratulations to the Class of 2026. Further information on our Sixth Form performance measures can be found on the Department for Education's School and College Performance website.

It is for the applicant family to choose which parent’s or carer’s details are to be included on the application form. In order to meet the conditions (section 11. below) for offering places when the number of applicants is more than the number of Foundation Places, the named parent or carer should normally be the parent or carer (when there is more than one in the family structure) whose minister can certify that they are practising members of their church or congregation. 6. Definitions For the purpose of this Admission Policy: ‘Family’ refers to the child and the ONE named parent or carer mentioned above with whom the child is normally resident. ‘Sibling’ refers to brothers and sisters (blood relatives), step-siblings, adopted and long-term foster children living at the same address. A ‘Looked After Child’ is a child who is (a) in the care of a Local Authority, or (b) being provided with accommodation by a Local Authority in the exercise of their social services functions (see definition in section 22(1) of the Children Act 1989) at the time of applying to the school. A ‘Previously Looked After Child’ is a child who was looked after immediately prior to being adopted, including Internationally Adopted Previously Looked After Children (IAPLAC). or who became subject to a child arrangement order under the Children & Families Act 2014, or special guardianship order. The Governors will require written confirmation (e.g. through written confirmation from the Local Authority) that the child is looked after, or previously looked after, and will be so at the time of making an application to the school. ‘Involvement’ is any activity (practical, social, educational, cultural or spiritual) which is an outward expression of the family’s participation in the life of the church to which they belong. It excludes any practical or financial support given to the school or any associated organisation, including any religious authority. Where percentages used in this policy do not produce whole numbers, 0.5 or more will be rounded up and less than 0.5 will be rounded down. 7. Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCP’s) Parents of pupils who have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) are required to apply for school places separately through the Local Authority, from whom advice is available. If a child with an EHCP, is placed in the school by the local authority before the normal admission round, the number of places available to other applicants will be reduced. The Governors will admit all those pupils whose EHCP, names the School (All schools are consulted by the LA prior to the school being named). 8. Looked After Children The highest priority is given to Looked After and Previously Looked After Children – with supporting evidence from their Local Authority (as defined in section 6 above). 9. Exceptional and professionally supported medical or social need. This must be supported by written evidence at the time of application, e.g. from a specialist health professional, social worker or other care professional. The evidence must set out the reasons why this school is the most suitable school and the difficulties that would be caused if the child had to attend another school. 10. (ii) In addition, whether Anglican or not, confirmation of membership of the applicant’s Family in the relevant church will be sought from the priest or minister concerned, who will also be required to give a reference in writing stating the frequency of church attendance by the Family, and give information about the involvement of the Family in church life. (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) Children who attend church worship weekly with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer is actively involved with them in church life. “Actively involved” indicates that this activity is likely to be frequent (at least fortnightly), well established (for at least 1 year) and to carry with it some responsibility within the church. (iii) Children who attend church worship fortnightly with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer is actively involved with them in church life. “Actively involved” indicates that this activity is likely to be frequent (fortnightly), well established (for at least 1 year) and carry with it some responsibility within the church. (iv) Children who attend church worship weekly, fortnightly or less frequently with the named parent or carer and whose named parent or carer has some involvement with them in church life. “Some involvement” indicates that this activity is likely to be less frequent (monthly), less well established (for less than a year) and more passive (e.g. attending a meeting). (v) Children who attend church with the named parent or carer. Note: In any of the categories 11c (i- v) above where there are more applicants than places remaining available, places will be offered to the children whose named parent or carer has the greater level of responsibility and involvement. Where two or more named parents or carers have an identical level of responsibility and involvement, places will be offered according to the nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3 above. Unsuccessful applicants for Foundation Places will be considered under the Open Place criteria. If the Foundation Places overall are undersubscribed, those remaining unfilled will become Open Places. Parents are asked to note that because Scouts and Guides are frequently more secular than religious organisations, membership of these groups will not be regarded as active involvement, unless it can be clearly demonstrated that it is an integral part of church life. 12. Open Places The Governing Body has designated 50% of the available places as Open Places after any children admitted who have an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan which names the school (see 7 above), Looked After and Previously Looked After Children (see 8. above), Children of Staff and Governors’ Places. In the event of the School being oversubscribed by Open Place applicants, priority will be given to those who live in the area defined in section 3 (above) and who are not offered a Foundation Place, but whose parents have chosen the school for the type of education it provides. St John’s Church of England Primary School, Shirley b. The Minster Church of England Primary School, Croydon c. St Mark’s Church of England Primary Academy, South Norwood d. Christ Church Church of England Primary School, Purley e. All Saints Church of England Primary School, Upper Norwood f. Coulsdon Church of England Primary School, Coulsdon g. Holy Trinity Church of England Primary School, Sutton h. All Saints Carshalton Church of England Primary School, Carshalton i. All Saints Benhilton Church of England Primary School, Sutton j. St Dunstan’s Church of England Primary School, Cheam If the number of applicants exceeds 25% places will be allocated according to the following criteria: (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) Remaining places will be allocated in strict rotation between applications for children from the above schools which must be specified on the Supplementary Information Form (SIF). Where the number of applications from a school exceeds the places allocated to that school then places will be offered according to the nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3 above. If the places reserved for applications for children from the above feeder schools are undersubscribed they will then become Local Places. b) Local Places Half of the Open places (i.e. 25% of available places) are open for applications for any child. If the number of applicants exceeds 25%, places will be allocated according to the following criteria: (i) Siblings of pupils who will be attending the School, including the Sixth Form, at the time of the proposed admission. (ii) The nearness of the home to the school within the area defined in Section 3. 13. Governors’ Places Governors may allocate a small number of places on compassionate grounds for social and medical need or for a child attending church regularly but unsupported by family. Those applying under this category should state this on the Supplementary Information Form (SIF) at the time of application and supply in writing relevant supporting professional evidence. Governors are able to allocate compassionate places irrespective of whether the school is oversubscribed by applicants who meet the criteria listed. Sixth Form Admissions Admissions criteria for external applicants wishing to attend the Archbishop Tenison’s Sixth Form are published on the school website and available from the school office. 20. Supplementary Information Form (SIF) Failure to return the Supplementary Information Form (SIF) by the published deadline will mean that applicants cannot be considered for a place under the Foundation Place criteria or the Feeder School criteria, and the application will be dealt with under the Local Place criteria. 21.
